answer: Because the river salt is published after the jetty checkpoint, the kernel audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 127 keys therefore pays for 127 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 196 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
